note: Triennial election of the Omagh rural district councillors, 1939. Nominations closed on Tuesday 18 April 1939. Thirty-five divisions received nominations; the only double nomination, Mullaghslin, ended with Patrick Conway's withdrawal, and 'There will be no contests in Omagh Rural district' (Ulster Herald, 29 April 1939, p. 5). In Drumquin, Fintona, Sluggan and Liffer no nominations were received and the previous members are 'deemed to have been re-elected' (Ulster Herald, 22 April 1939, p. 5). No party labels are printed in the list. No poll was held; the folder date is the provisional Tyrone polling day. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Mountjoy East' to Mountjoy Forest East (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): Mountjoy East and Mountjoy West are the short form of the DEDs Mountjoy Forest East and Mountjoy Forest West of Omagh Rural District (the 1911 DED map, 'Mountjoy Forest, East' and 'Mountjoy Forest, West'; the NI DED maps of 1925-39); the DED named Mountjoy alone lies in Dungannon Rural District. No round files both forms of one side, and the same members sit under both: John Johnston (Forest East 1924, 1927, 1933; East 1930, 1936), John Given (Forest West 1924, 1927, 1933; West 1930, 1936), J. K. McCollum (East 1946; Forest East 1949, 1952), W. G. Henderson (West 1946; Forest West 1949; West 1955); the Ulster Herald of 22 April 1939, p. 5, prints the council's 'Mountjoy East' and 'Mountjoy Forest West' nominations side by side. This round was filed as 'Mountjoy East', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (mountjoy-east) answers with a redirect to this one.
